biography:
Nacho Tuñon's racing journey began on the sun-baked karting tracks of Valencia. Unlike many drivers who were practically born into racing families, Nacho discovered his passion almost by accident. At 14, while working part-time at a local kart track, he took a discarded kart for a spin and immediately felt an electrifying connection. His natural aggression and raw talent quickly caught the eye of a local karting team owner. 

Nacho dedicated himself entirely to karting, spending countless hours honing his skills. A defining moment came during the Valencian Karting Championship when, despite starting near the back of the grid due to a mechanical failure, he fought his way to victory, showcasing his incredible overtaking ability and never-say-die attitude. That win earned him a spot with the Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Direct team, marking his entry into competitive racing at a higher level.

While he hasn't achieved international acclaim, Nacho is a formidable presence in the Spanish karting scene. He remains fiercely competitive and dedicated, constantly pushing himself to improve. Though opportunities for higher-tier racing have been limited, Nacho's passion and commitment to karting remain unwavering. He's currently aiming to secure another championship title with Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Direct, proving that talent and determination can overcome any obstacle.
drivingStyle: Nacho's driving style is characterized by its raw aggression and relentless pursuit of speed. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and daring overtakes, often pushing the limits of his kart and tires. While his aggressive approach can sometimes lead to mistakes, it also allows him to extract maximum performance from his machine. He favors a high-risk, high-reward strategy, always searching for an opportunity to gain an advantage. Tire management is his weakness, often burning through his rubber early in the race.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 Valencian Karting Championship after a season-long battle with Isabella Vargas. He secured the title in the final race with a daring last-lap overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the 2020 Spanish National Karting Championship, costing him the championship title. A mechanical failure caused the crash.
